is_anopheles.evidence: Study evaluated populations of Anopheles coluzzii and Anopheles gambiae s.l. collected in Benin (Page 1, 4, 8 Table 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotyped the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) kdr mutation using PCR-PASA (Page 5, Page 9 Table 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on Page 9 reports exact counts and percentages of L1014F/L1014F, L1014L/L1014F, and L1014L/L1014L genotypes for An. coluzzii in four localities (Cotonou, Sô-Ava, Zagnanado, Kétou).

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae were sampled in four localities in southern Benin between May 2015 and October 2017 and reared to adults for molecular analysis (Page 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study involving field mosquito collection, pesticide surveys, and laboratory molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: Table 2 on Page 8 provides collection sites/villages with exact GPS coordinates (latitude and longitude) across Cotonou, Sô-Ava, Kétou, and Zagnanado.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito larvae were collected from May 2015 to October 2017 (Page 4), spanning a window of 2.5 years.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper describes original field sampling and genotyping conducted by CREC between 2015 and 2017.

supplement.evidence: All primary genotype counts, species identification results, and site GPS coordinates are included in Tables 2 and 3 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated pesticide usage and the genetic structure of Anopheles coluzzii populations across four localities in southern Benin (Cotonou, Sô-Ava, Kétou, Zagnanado). Mosquito larvae were collected between May 2015 and October 2017. A total of 404 An. coluzzii were genotyped for the Vgsc L1014F kdr mutation, showing high frequencies of the resistant L1014F allele across all sites.
